lists.content:
• Set technical direction for complex frontend product areas that span multiple teams, from problem definition through architecture, rollout, and iteration.
  • Find the most important frontend problems across teams, including ones that aren’t on anyone’s roadmap. Build the case for solving them and get teams aligned.
  • Make architecture decisions with long-term consequences. These cover component design, application state, data fetching, API contracts, error handling, and performance. Document the tradeoffs so others can build on them.
  • Lead the evolution of our shared frontend architecture and design system, including our ongoing design-system modernization, and drive adoption across teams.
  • Work with backend engineers and other technical leads to define clear boundaries and contracts between frontend and backend systems.
  • Work with Product and Design leaders on scope, sequencing, and product direction. Help them understand the technical options and what each one means for users.
  • Translate complex clinical, operational, and patient workflows into interfaces that are intuitive, reliable, and safe.
  • Balance near-term delivery against long-term engineering health, and make those tradeoffs visible to the people affected.
  • Raise the quality bar across frontend in testing, accessibility, observability, reliability, and performance. Own production outcomes for the systems you lead.
  • Use user feedback, product data, and operational metrics to judge whether what we shipped worked, and decide where to go next.
  • Help other engineers, including senior engineers, make better technical decisions through mentorship, design reviews, and day-to-day collaboration.
  • Write production code, especially on the most consequential and highest-risk parts of the work.
  • Participate in on-call rotations and take ownership of the health of the systems your teams operate.

lists.text: What You'll Bring to the Team
lists.content:
• Significant recent experience building and owning production applications with React and TypeScript, with deep expertise in frontend architecture.
  • A track record of setting technical direction for frontend work that spanned multiple teams or systems, and seeing it through to adoption.
  • Experience architecting complex, stateful product workflows, such as multi-step forms, scheduling, messaging, queues, or data-dense applications.
  • Deep fundamentals in component architecture, state management, API design and integration, server-side rendering, accessibility, performance, testing, and failure-state design.
  • Experience making architecture decisions with long-term consequences. You should be able to explain what you considered, what you traded off, and what you’d do differently.
  • Experience owning the reliability and production health of what you and your teams ship, including observability, incident response, and follow-through after launch.
  • A track record of shaping product direction with Product and Design, including disagreeing constructively when the stakes were high.
  • Evidence of influencing engineers and stakeholders outside your own team without relying on authority.
  • Experience improving how other engineers work, through shared patterns, design systems, standards, tooling, or mentorship.
  • The ability to explain technical decisions and tradeoffs clearly to engineers, non-engineering partners, and leadership.
  • Evidence of connecting technical work to measurable outcomes for users or the business.

• Experience in healthcare, telehealth, clinical workflows, or another highly regulated industry.
  • Experience building software for specialized internal or operational users, such as clinicians, support teams, financial operators, or other domain experts.
  • Experience leading a design-system modernization or a large-scale frontend migration.
  • Familiarity with tools such as Turborepo, TanStack Query, React Aria, Playwright, Storybook, or Chromatic.
  • Experience using AI or automation to improve product workflows or engineering workflows.

  • Paid parental leave + Fertility benefits

The Role:
As a Staff Software Engineer/Tech Lead on our Patient Experience team, you’ll serve as a technical and architectural leader for the systems that help patients discover, start, and continue their care with Ro. You'll be responsible for the patient-facing platform that supports patients taking the first steps in their patient journey - and the second, and the tenth, and the 100th. Rather than building one-off experiments, you’ll design the architecture and technical foundations that allow us to continuously iterate on and personalize intake for patients as we learn more about their needs. lists.content:
• Translate patient and growth opportunities into technical strategy, partnering with product and engineering to determine how systems should evolve to support the outcomes we’re trying to achieve.
  • Lead complex, backend-oriented engineering work across healthcare intake and prescription flows, commerce, merchandising, subscriptions, renewals, and related patient experiences.
  • Shape ambiguous problems from the earliest stages, bringing systems thinking and technical judgment into product decisions rather than engaging only once requirements have been defined.
  • Elevate the team’s technical and product thinking, helping engineers reason about both the systems underneath an experience and the patient and business outcomes those systems enable.

lists.text: What You’ll Bring to the Team:

  • Experience leading technical work for consumer-facing growth experiences, such as acquisition, onboarding, conversion, merchandising, subscriptions, retention, or renewal.

  • The ability to move fluidly between product and systems thinking, understanding the patient experience while reasoning deeply about the architecture that enables it.
  • Comfort operating in ambiguous, cross-functional environments, creating clarity, navigating tradeoffs, and driving complex technical work forward.

  • Strong backend engineering fundamentals and experience building complex, production systems, with proficiency in Python or enough experience with similar languages to quickly become effective in Ro’s Python-based stack.

descriptionPlain:
Ro is a direct-to-patient healthcare company with a mission of helping patients achieve their health goals by delivering the easiest, most effective care possible. Ro is the only company to offer nationwide telehealth, labs, and pharmacy services. This is enabled by Ro's vertically integrated platform that helps patients achieve their goals through a convenient, end-to-end healthcare experience spanning from diagnosis, to delivery of medication, to ongoing care. Since 2017, Ro has helped millions of patients in nearly every single county in the United States, including 99% of primary care deserts.
 
Ro is consistently recognized as a top workplace in Health Care, in New York, and for Women and Parents—earning more than 20 honors from Fortune, Great Place to Work, and PEOPLE since 2021. In 2025 alone, we ranked top 5 among medium workplaces in Health Care and New York, and top 50 nationwide.


As a Temporary R&D Engineer on Ro’s Product Development team, you will help design, optimize, validate, and document the processes required to bring new products from development through launch and into repeatable pharmacy operations.
You will work at the intersection of Product Development and Pharmacy Operations, partnering closely with Pharmacy, Pharmacy Compliance, Quality/Regulatory, Supply Chain, and other cross-functional teams to translate product requirements into scalable, reliable, and well-controlled compounding processes.
This role will have a strong focus on process development, scale-up, process optimization, and technical documentation. You will evaluate existing and proposed workflows, identify process risks and opportunities for improvement, develop standardized processes, and support pilot and production activities to ensure new products can be consistently and efficiently produced at the required quality standards.
As a temporary member of the team, you will be expected to ramp quickly, independently drive defined workstreams, and leave behind robust processes, documentation, and tools that enable teams to operate effectively after the engagement.

Since 2017, Ro has helped millions of patients in nearly every single county in the United States, including 99% of primary care deserts.
 
Ro is consistently recognized as a top workplace in Health Care, in New York, and for Women and Parents—earning more than 20 honors from Fortune, Great Place to Work, and PEOPLE since 2021. In 2025 alone, we ranked top 5 among medium workplaces in Health Care and New York, and top 50 nationwide.

As a Temporary R&D Engineer on Ro’s Product Development team, you will help design, optimize, validate, and document the processes required to bring new products from development through launch and into repeatable pharmacy operations.

You will work at the intersection of Product Development and Pharmacy Operations, partnering closely with Pharmacy, Pharmacy Compliance, Quality/Regulatory, Supply Chain, and other cross-functional teams to translate product requirements into scalable, reliable, and well-controlled compounding processes.

This role will have a strong focus on process development, scale-up, process optimization, and technical documentation. You will evaluate existing and proposed workflows, identify process risks and opportunities for improvement, develop standardized processes, and support pilot and production activities to ensure new products can be consistently and efficiently produced at the required quality standards.

As a temporary member of the team, you will be expected to ramp quickly, independently drive defined workstreams, and leave behind robust processes, documentation, and tools that enable teams to operate effectively after the engagement.

lists.content:
• Develop and optimize processes for new and existing products, translating product and formulation requirements into repeatable compounding workflows that can be successfully executed within pharmacy operations.

  • Lead process scale-up and technology transfer, partnering with Product Development and Pharmacy teams to transition products from lab or pilot development into production / compounding.

  • Map and assess current-state processes to identify bottlenecks, sources of variability, operational risks, and opportunities to improve efficiency, quality, and scalability.

  • Design future-state processes and establish appropriate process parameters, controls, equipment requirements, material flows, and operating procedures.

  • Plan and execute process trials, pilot runs, engineering batches, and first production runs to evaluate process performance and resolve technical issues prior to or during launch.

  • Analyze process performance and troubleshoot issues using data and structured problem-solving methodologies to identify root causes and implement corrective or preventive improvements.

  • Develop and maintain technical documentation, including process maps, SOPs, work instructions, process specifications, batch documentation, equipment requirements, and other materials required to support reliable execution.

  • Identify critical process parameters and risks and partner with Quality, Compliance, and Pharmacy stakeholders to establish appropriate controls and acceptance criteria.

  • Evaluate equipment and compounding capabilities and recommend solutions that improve process reliability, throughput, ergonomics, quality, or scalability.

  • Support new product launches by developing process readiness plans, identifying dependencies and risks, and ensuring operational requirements are addressed before launch.

  • Partner cross-functionally with Product Development, Pharmacy Operations, Pharmacy Compliance, Quality/Regulatory, Supply Chain, and external partners to drive projects from development through implementation.

  • Manage multiple workstreams and timelines, proactively communicating risks, dependencies, decisions, and progress to key stakeholders.

  • Drive continuous improvement by identifying opportunities to simplify workflows, reduce variability and waste, improve cycle time, and increase process capability.

  • Transfer knowledge to operational teams through clear documentation, training, and structured handoffs to ensure new or improved processes are sustainable.

  • Stay informed on relevant compounding, pharmacy, manufacturing, automation, and process-engineering technologies and capabilities.

  • Travel as needed to Ro pharmacy locations, suppliers, manufacturers, or other partners to support development, testing, scale-up, and implementation activities.

lists.text: What You’ll Bring to the Team:
lists.content:
• Bachelor’s degree in Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, or a related technical field.

  • 3+ years of experience in process engineering, manufacturing engineering, process development, technical operations, or a related role, preferably within pharmaceuticals, compounding, consumer health, medical devices, cosmetics, food, or another regulated manufacturing environment.

  • Hands-on experience developing and scaling processes, including pilot activities, production trials, process qualification, technology transfer, or new product introduction.

  • Strong process-engineering fundamentals, with experience defining process parameters, evaluating process capability, identifying sources of variability, and designing robust production workflows.

  • Experience with structured problem solving and continuous improvement, including root-cause analysis, process mapping, FMEA, Lean/Six Sigma, DOE, or similar methodologies.

  • Strong analytical skills and the ability to use data to evaluate process performance, identify trends, and make recommendations.

  • Experience creating technical documentation, including SOPs, work instructions, process flows, specifications, protocols, and technical reports.

  • Excellent project and timeline management skills, with the ability to independently manage multiple projects and priorities in a fast-paced environment.

descriptionBody:
As a Temporary R&D Engineer on Ro’s Product Development team, you will help design, optimize, validate, and document the processes required to bring new products from development through launch and into repeatable pharmacy operations.

You will work at the intersection of Product Development and Pharmacy Operations, partnering closely with Pharmacy, Pharmacy Compliance, Quality/Regulatory, Supply Chain, and other cross-functional teams to translate product requirements into scalable, reliable, and well-controlled compounding processes.

This role will have a strong focus on process development, scale-up, process optimization, and technical documentation. You will evaluate existing and proposed workflows, identify process risks and opportunities for improvement, develop standardized processes, and support pilot and production activities to ensure new products can be consistently and efficiently produced at the required quality standards.

As a temporary member of the team, you will be expected to ramp quickly, independently drive defined workstreams, and leave behind robust processes, documentation, and tools that enable teams to operate effectively after the engagement.

RPM is part of the provider network affiliated with Ro, a direct-to-patient healthcare company. RPM providers benefit from using technology, tools, and solutions designed to support safe and appropriate care, reduce administrative burden, and help them seamlessly connect with patients throughout their care journeys. descriptionPlain:
Ro is a direct-to-patient healthcare company with a mission of helping patients achieve their health goals by delivering the easiest, most effective care possible. Ro is the only company to offer nationwide telehealth, labs, and pharmacy services. This is enabled by Ro's vertically integrated platform that helps patients achieve their goals through a convenient, end-to-end healthcare experience spanning from diagnosis, to delivery of medication, to ongoing care. Since 2017, Ro has helped millions of patients in nearly every single county in the United States, including 99% of primary care deserts.
 
Ro is consistently recognized as a top workplace in Health Care, in New York, and for Women and Parents—earning more than 20 honors from Fortune, Great Place to Work, and PEOPLE since 2021. In 2025 alone, we ranked top 5 among medium workplaces in Health Care and New York, and top 50 nationwide.


As the VP of Pharmacy Operations, you will lead end-to-end fulfillment strategy and execution across a multi-site pharmacy network, with full ownership of operational performance, service levels, patient experience, regulatory compliance, and financial outcomes. You will partner closely with leaders across Supply Chain, Tech, Finance, Quality  & Safety, Compounding, and Patient Experience teams to build a scalable, efficient, and patient-centric operation. Reporting to the Chief Pharmacy & Logistics Officer, you will play a critical role in shaping the future of pharmacy operations at Ro, driving innovation through automation, regionalization, and continuous improvement.  The ideal candidate  brings a systems-thinking mindset, strong operational rigor, exceptional interpersonal skills, and the ability to lead high-performing teams in a complex, regulated environment.

This role is embedded onsite, with its primary location at our Romeoville, IL facility, and requires regular travel to other pharmacy sites, including Florida and California.

lists.content:
• Own operational performance management across the pharmacy network through KPI reporting, forecasting, and standardized operating mechanisms that drive throughput, quality, delivery reliability, and unit economics
  • Drive large-scale operational excellence and continuous improvement initiatives that enhance scalability, improve patient outcomes and delivery experience, reduce costs and strengthen operational resilience
  • Own the strategy and performance of automation systems, driving uptime, throughput optimization, and capital efficiency across the network
  • Lead network optimization and routing strategies in partnership with Supply Chain and Logistics teams to improve delivery speed, routing efficiency, fulfillment accuracy, and overall network performance 
  • Establish and execute workforce planning & strategy, aligning staffing models with demand forecasts, automation capabilities, productivity targets, and budget
  • Build, lead and develop a high-performing operations organization through strong leadership, employee engagement, talent development, and a culture of accountability and continuous improvement
  • Collaborate closely with cross-functional partners to ensure seamless execution from production through final-mile delivery
  • Own pharmacy licensing strategy and execution across all operating states, ensuring proactive management of new licenses, renewals, and related regulatory requirements in partnership with Legal and Compliance teams to support uninterrupted operations
  • Ensure compliance with all applicable FDA, Board of Pharmacy, OSHA, quality, safety, and regulatory requirements through rigorous operational controls and strong cross-functional partnership with Quality, People, and Compliance teams
  • Lead organizational transformation and change management initiatives related to automation, process redesign, operational scaling, and evolving business priorities
  • Serve as a key operational leader to executive stakeholders, translating business strategy into scalable operational capabilities and execution plans

• 12+ years of experience in pharmacy operations, fulfillment, or supply chain, with significant multi-site leadership experience
  • Proven track record of leading large-scale mail-order pharmacy operations or high volume fulfillment operations
  • Deep experience in workforce planning, labor optimization, and scaling operations in high-growth environments
  • Strong understanding of automation and systems integration, with experience leading implementation or optimization initiatives
  • Experience operating in highly regulated environments, with knowledge of pharmacy licensing, compliance, and quality standards
  • Data-driven leader with strong financial and analytical acumen, including ownership of unit economics and operational KPIs
  • Demonstrated ability to influence and align cross-functional stakeholders at all levels, including executive leadership
  • Strong people leadership skills, with experience in building, developing, and retaining high-performing teams

• Full medical, dental, and vision insurance + OneMedical membership

  • Healthcare and Dependent Care FSA

  • 401(k) with company match

  • Flexible PTO

  • Wellbeing + Learning & Growth stipends

  • Paid parental leave + Fertility benefits

  • Pet insurance

  • Student loan refinancing

  • Virtual resources for mindfulness, counseling, and fitness

Ro is a direct-to-patient healthcare company with a mission of helping patients achieve their health goals by delivering the easiest, most effective care possible. Ro is the only company to offer nationwide telehealth, labs, and pharmacy services. This is enabled by Ro's vertically integrated platform that helps patients achieve their goals through a convenient, end-to-end healthcare experience spanning from diagnosis, to delivery of medication, to ongoing care. Since 2017, Ro has helped millions of patients in nearly every single county in the United States, including 99% of primary care deserts.
 
Ro is consistently recognized as a top workplace in Health Care, in New York, and for Women and Parents—earning more than 20 honors from Fortune, Great Place to Work, and PEOPLE since 2021. In 2025 alone, we ranked top 5 among medium workplaces in Health Care and New York, and top 50 nationwide.


As a Warehouse Associate, you will play a key role in the day-to-day operations of our Torrance facility. You will be responsible for picking and packing items for shipment, operating forklifts and pallet jacks, maintaining organized inventory, and supporting inbound and outbound logistics. You will help ensure accuracy in inventory counts and work to maintain a clean, safe, and efficient warehouse environment. You’re a versatile team player who thrives in a fast-paced setting and takes pride in organization and operational precision.
 
We are looking for a Warehouse Associate with full-time availability, Monday - Friday, 8:30am - 5pm. This position is located on-site in Torrance, California.

lists.content:
• Support daily warehouse activities including receiving, stocking, picking, packing, and shipping inventory
  • Package and ship patient orders accurately and efficiently in accordance with company SOPs
  • Operate warehouse equipment including forklifts and pallet jacks
  • Receive and inspect inbound inventory and ensure accurate stocking of materials
  • Perform regular inventory cycle counts and assist in reconciliation processes
  • Monitor supply levels during daily operations and report low stock to team leads or management
  • Maintain cleanliness and organization across all warehouse areas
  • Collaborate with warehouse team members to complete daily tasks and meet shipping deadlines
  • Follow established workflows and operational protocols to ensure safety, quality, and productivity standards
  • Communicate clearly and respectfully with team members to ensure a smooth and coordinated workflow
  • Perform other warehouse-related tasks as assigned by supervisors or team leads

lists.text: What You’ll Bring to the Team:
lists.content:
• Strong attention to detail with a commitment to accuracy and quality control
  • Ability to follow safety protocols and maintain a clean, organized work area
  • Comfortable working in a fast-paced environment and adapting to changing priorities
  • Effective communication skills and the ability to work collaboratively with cross-functional teams
  • Willingness to learn and take direction, with a positive attitude and proactive approach to problem-solving
  • Dependable and punctual, with a strong work ethic and team-oriented mindset
  • Long periods of standing, must be able to bend at the waist and knee, occasionally lift up to 50 lbs
  • Forklift experience required

• Full medical, dental, and vision insurance + OneMedical membership
  • Healthcare and Dependent Care FSA
  • 401(k) with company match
  • Flexible PTO
  • Wellbeing + Learning & Growth reimbursements
  • Paid parental leave + Fertility benefits
  • Pet insurance
  • Student loan refinancing
  • Virtual resources for mindfulness, counseling, and fitness
